καὶ ἡμῖν ἀφῆκε τὰ ἁμαρτήματα ὁ Θεός. πῶς δὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἐν Χριστῷ ἐχαρίσατο ἡμῖν τὰ
ἁμαρτήματα; ἢ ὅτι ἐν Χριστῷ ὢν ὁ πατὴρ ἀφῆκεν ἡμῖν τὰ παραπτώματα; ἐν Χριστῷ
δὲ ἐχαρίσατο ἡμῖν καὶ τὰ ἀγαθά, εἴ γε ἐν Χριστῷ σοφία ἐστὶν ἣν ἐχαρίσατο ἡμῖν καὶ
ἀλήθεια καὶ δικαιοσύνη. 24 Eph. v3, 4 [πορνεία δὲ καὶ ἀκαθαρσία πᾶσα ἢ πλεονεξία
μηδὲ ὀνομαζέσθω ἐν ὑμῖν, καθὼς πρέπει ἁγίοις, καὶ αἰσχρότης καὶ μωρολογία ἢ
εὐτραπελία, ἃ οὐκ ἀνῆκεν, ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον εὐχαριστία.] [Ὠριγένης δέ φησιν] ἡ μὲν
πρὸς πόρνην κοινωνία κατὰ τὸ ἔθος τῆς γραφῆς πορνεία ὀνομάζεται· πᾶσα δὲ ἡ κατὰ
τὸν τόπον τῶν σαρκικῶν γαργαλισμῶν ἁμαρτία, οὐ μόνον κατὰ τὰς μοιχείας καὶ
παιδοφθορίας ἀλλὰ καὶ κατὰ τὰ ἄλλα ὅσα ἐπενόησεν ἡ ἀνθρωπίνη ἀκολασία ἐν
διαφόροις καὶ παντοδαπαῖς παρατριβαῖς, ἀκαθαρσία γενικῶς ὠνόμασται. τὴν
πλεονεξίαν δὲ ἤτοι ἁπλούστερον ἐκδεκτέον, ἤ, ὡς ἐν ἄλλοις παρεστήσαμεν, τὴν
μοιχείαν, ὅτε καὶ ἐχρησάμεθα τῷ μὴ ὑπερβαίνειν καὶ πλεονεκτεῖν ἕκα τον τὸν
ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ. πᾶσαν δὲ τὴν ἀκαθαρσίαν δεῖ φυλάξασθαι, ἐπεὶ τοῦτο πρέπει ἁγίοις.
αἰσχρότης δέ τις ἔστι καθ' ἕκαστον εἶδος ἀκολασίας· καὶ ὁμοίως γε αἰσχρότης ἐστὶ
καὶ ἀκαθαρσία· ἐμφαίνει γὰρ καὶ τὸ ἀκάθαρτον καὶ τὸ αἰσχρὸν ἑκάστη πρᾶξις ἡ κατὰ
τὸν τόπον τῆς εἰς τὸ ἀποκρίνειν ἐνεργείας· ταῦτα δὲ ἐπὶ τῶν παρὰ φύσιν λεκτέον,
οὐκ ἐπὶ τοῦ γάμου. ἴδωμεν δὲ τίς καὶ ἡ μωρολογία, ἣν καὶ αὐτὴν οὐδὲ ὀνομάζεσθαι
χρὴ ἐν τοῖς ἁγίοις. ὁ μὲν οὖν τις φήσει, ἁπλούστερον τὴν λέξιν ἐξειληφώς,
μωρολογίαν εἶναι τὴν ἀσκουμένην ὑπὸ τῶν βωμολόχων καὶ γελωτοποιῶν. ὅρα δὲ εἰ
μὴ μωρολο γεῖν λεκτέον καὶ τοὺς ὁτιδήποτε σοφίας καὶ συνέσεως ἠλλοτριωμένους
πάντας, καὶ μωρὸν ἐν τοῖς δογματιζομένοις ὑπ' αὐτῶν. δόξει δὲ συνᾴδειν τῷ
ἁπλούστερον ἐκδέξασθαι τὴν μωρολογίαν ἡ ἐπιφερομένη αὐτῇ εὐτραπελία, ἥντινα ἡ
τῶν ἰδιωτῶν συνήθεια τάσσει ἐπὶ τῶν οὐ μόνον ἀπὸ μωρολογίας ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀφ'
οἱασδήποτε αἰτίας γέλωτα κινούντων. οὐκ ἀνῆκε δὲ τοῖς ἁγίοις οὐδὲ αὕτη, ἀλλὰ
μᾶλλον ἡ ἐν πᾶσι πρὸς Θεὸν εὐχα ριστία, ἤγουν εὐχαριστία καθ' ἣν εὐχαρίτους καὶ
χαρίεντάς τινάς φαμεν. μωρό λογον μὲν οὖν καὶ εὐτράπελον οὐ δεῖ εἶναι, εὐχάριτον
δὲ καὶ χαρίεντα· καὶ ἐπεὶ ἀσύνηθές ἐστι τὸ εἰπεῖν «ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον εὐχαριτία,» τάχα
ἀντὶ τούτου ἐχρή σατο τῇ ἐπ' ἄλλου κειμένῃ λέξει καὶ εἶπεν, ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον

«εὐχαρίστου» τοὺς ἀπὸ Ἑβραίων χρῆσθαι ἀντὶ τῆς «εὐχαριτίας» καὶ «εὐχαρίτου»·

ἐγείρει ἀνδρὶ δόξαν ἀντὶ τοῦ «εὐχάριτος γυνή»· βιάζεσθαι δὲ ἂν ἐδόξαμεν τὸ γυνὴ
εὐχάρι το ἀντὶ τοῦ «εὐχάριτος» ἐκλαμβάνοντες, εἰ μὴ αἱ λοιπαὶ ἐκδόσεις συνῇδον
ταύτῃ τῇ ἐκδοχῇ. ὁ μὲν γὰρ Ἀκύλας οὕτως ἡρμήνευσεν γυνὴ χάριτο ἀντέχεται
δόξη , Θεοδοτίων δὲ καὶ Σύμμαχος γυνὴ χάριτο ἀνθέξεται δόξη . [v 5] τοῦτο γάρ ἐστε
γινώσκοντες, ὅτι πᾶς πόρνος ἢ ἀκάθαρτος ἢ πλεονέκτης, ὅς ἐστιν εἰδωλολάτρης, οὐκ
ἔχει κληρονομίαν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ Θεοῦ. παρατηρητέον ὅτι ἓξ
ἀπαγορεύσας ἁμαρτήματα, πορνείαν καὶ ἀκαθαρσίαν καὶ πλεονεξίαν καὶ αἰσχρότητα
καὶ μωρολογίαν καὶ εὐτραπελίαν, οὐ κατὰ τὰ ἓξ ἐπιφέρει ὥστε τὸν ἐνεχόμενόν τινι
αὐτῶν μὴ ἔχειν κληρονομίαν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ Θεοῦ, ἀλλὰ τρία, λέγω
δὲ πορνείαν καὶ ἀκαθαρσίαν πᾶσαν καὶ πλεονεξίαν. εἰ γὰρ μὴ εἶχον κληρονομίαν ἐν
τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ Θεοῦ καὶ ὁ μωρολογίᾳ καὶ εὐτραπελίᾳ ἔνοχος,
ὠμότερον ἄν τινι ἐφαίνετο τὸ κατὰ τὴν κρίσιν ἐπὶ μηδενὶ συγγινώσκουσαν τῇ
ἀσθενεῖ ἡμῶν φύσει. ἄλλως μὲν γὰρ οὐδὲ ταῦτα ἀνῆκεν, πλὴν οὐχ ὥστε
πραττομένων αὐτῶν ἐκπίπτειν τινὰ τῆς κληρονομίας τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ Θεοῦ. λείπει
καὶ περὶ τῆς αἰσχρότητος ἐπιστῆσαι. δόξαις ἄρ' ἂν εὔλογον εἶναι τὸ λέγεσθαι πᾶς
πόρνος ἢ ἀκάθαρτος ἢ πλεονέκτης ἢ αἰσχρὸς οὐκ ἔχει κληρονομίαν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ
τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ Θεοῦ. ἀλλὰ μήποτε ἡ αἰσχρότης ἐστὶν ἐν τῷ κατὰ τὸ κρυπτὸν μόνον
παθητικῶς μεμολυσμένῳ, ᾗ καὶ πυρωθείς τις ἀνέστειλεν τὴν ἐπὶ τὴν πορνείαν ἢ τὴν
ἐπὶ τὴν ἀκαθαρσίαν ὁρμήν. καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἀνωτέρω δὲ τὰ μὲν κωλύοντα κληρονομίαν
pass_a_gloss: one another, will think it to be said equivalently to forgiving one another, most of all because of the as God in Christ forgave us, and will carry these things to the forgiveness of the sins, saying that we must forgive those sinning against us, as also God forgave us the sins. And how did God in Christ forgive us the sins? Or because the Father, being in Christ, forgave us the trespasses? And in Christ he also granted us the good things, if indeed in Christ is wisdom which he granted us, and truth and righteousness. [5:3-4] And fornication and all uncleanness or greed let it not even be named among you, as befits saints, and shamefulness and foolish talk or jesting, which are not fitting, but rather thanksgiving. Origen says: the fellowship with a harlot according to the custom of scripture is named fornication; and every sin according to the place of the fleshly ticklings, not only according to the adulteries and the boy-corruptions but also according to the other things as many as human licentiousness devised in different and all kinds of rubbings, has been named generically uncleanness. And the greed one must take either more simply, or, as we presented in other places, the adultery, when we also used the not to go beyond and defraud each his brother. And one must guard against all the uncleanness, since this befits saints. And there is a certain shamefulness according to each species of licentiousness; and likewise shamefulness is also uncleanness; for each act according to the place of the activity toward excreting shows both the unclean and the shameful; but these things must be said of the things against nature, not of marriage. And let us see what also the foolish talk is, which itself also must not even be named among the saints. One then will say, having taken the word more simply, foolish talk to be that practiced by the buffoons and laughter-makers. But see whether one must not say also all those estranged from any wisdom and understanding to talk foolishly, and foolish in the things laid down as doctrine by them. And the jesting brought on after it will seem to agree with taking the foolish talk more simply, which the usage of the unlearned ranks upon those moving laughter not only from foolish talk but also from any cause whatever. And neither does this befit the saints, but rather the thanksgiving toward God in all things, or rather thanksgiving according to which we call some gracious and charming. Therefore one must not be foolish-talking and jesting, but gracious and charming; and since it is unusual to say but rather graciousness, perhaps instead of this he used the word lying upon another thing and said but rather thanksgiving. And perhaps it is custom for those from the Hebrews to use the name of thanksgiving and thankful instead of graciousness and gracious; and such we thought to be also the thing said thus in Proverbs: a thankful woman raises glory for a husband, instead of gracious woman; but we would have seemed to force the a thankful woman, taking it instead of gracious, if the remaining editions did not agree with this interpretation. For Aquila interpreted thus: a woman of grace holds on to glory; and Theodotion and Symmachus: a woman of grace will hold on to glory. [5:5] For this you are knowing, that every fornicator or unclean or greedy one, who is an idolater, does not have inheritance in the kingdom of the Christ and God. One must observe that, having forbidden six sins, fornication and uncleanness and greed and shamefulness and foolish talk and jesting, he does not bring on according to the six so that the one held in one of them does not have inheritance in the kingdom of the Christ and God, but three, I mean fornication and all uncleanness and greed. For if also the one liable to foolish talk and jesting did not have inheritance in the kingdom of the Christ and God, the thing according to the judgment would appear to someone more savage, pardoning in nothing our weak nature. For otherwise neither are these fitting, but not so that, these being done, someone falls out of the inheritance of the Christ and God. It remains also to attend about the shamefulness. You might think then it reasonable that it be said every fornicator or unclean or greedy or shameful one does not have inheritance in the kingdom of the Christ and God. But perhaps the shamefulness is in the one stained passionately only according to the hidden, by which also someone, having been set on fire, held back the impulse toward fornication or toward uncleanness. And in the things above the things hindering inheritance
pass_b_english: another,” will think it is said with the same force as “forgiving one another,” chiefly because of “as God in Christ forgave us,” and will refer these words to the forgiveness of sins, saying that we must forgive those who sin against us, as God also forgave us our sins. But how did God in Christ forgive us our sins? Is it because the Father, being in Christ, forgave us our trespasses? Yet in Christ he also gave us good things, if indeed in Christ is the wisdom that he gave us, and truth and righteousness.

“But fornication and all uncleanness or greed must not even be named among you, as is fitting for saints; nor shamefulness and foolish talk or jesting, which are not fitting, but rather thanksgiving” (Ephesians 5:3–4). Origen says: by the custom of Scripture, intercourse with a prostitute is called fornication; but every sin in the region of fleshly titillation, not only adulteries and the corruption of boys but also all the other things that human licentiousness has devised in varied and manifold rubbings, has been named, as a class, uncleanness.

Greed must be understood either more simply or, as we have shown elsewhere, as adultery, where we also used the words “that no one go beyond and overreach his brother” (1 Thessalonians 4:6). All uncleanness must be guarded against, since this is what is fitting for saints. There is a kind of shamefulness in each form of licentiousness; and in the same way shamefulness is also uncleanness, for every act in the region whose work is excretion shows both the unclean and the shameful. But this must be said of acts against nature, not of marriage.

Let us see also what foolish talk is, which itself, too, must not even be named among the saints. Someone who takes the word more simply will say that foolish talk is what buffoons and jesters practice. But see whether we must not also say that all who are in any way estranged from wisdom and understanding talk foolishly, and that what they lay down as doctrine is foolish. The jesting that is joined to foolish talk will seem to agree with taking foolish talk more simply, for the usage of ordinary people applies the word to those who raise a laugh not only from foolish talk but from any cause at all. This too is not fitting for saints, but rather thanksgiving to God in all things, or else a “thanksgiving” that means grace, as when we call people gracious and charming.

So one must not be a foolish talker and a jester, but gracious and charming. And since it is unusual to say “but rather graciousness,” perhaps he used instead the word that belongs to something else and said “but rather thanksgiving.” Perhaps, too, those who come from the Hebrews are accustomed to use the words “thanksgiving” and “thankful” for “graciousness” and “gracious.” We thought that what is said in Proverbs is of this kind: “A thankful woman raises up glory for her husband,” in place of “a gracious woman.” But we would have seemed to force the text in taking “a thankful woman” as “a gracious woman,” if the other versions did not agree with this reading. For Aquila translated, “A woman of grace holds fast to glory,” and Theodotion and Symmachus, “A woman of grace will hold fast to glory” (Proverbs 11:16).

“For know this, that every fornicator or unclean or greedy person, who is an idolater, has no inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God” (Ephesians 5:5). We must observe that, having forbidden six sins (fornication, uncleanness, greed, shamefulness, foolish talk and jesting), he does not add of all six that whoever is guilty of any of them has no inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God, but of three, I mean fornication, all uncleanness and greed. For if the one guilty of foolish talk and jesting also had no inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God, the judgment would seem to some rather harsh, since it would pardon our weak nature in nothing. These things are not fitting either, it is true; but not so that by doing them anyone falls from the inheritance of Christ and God.

It remains to consider shamefulness as well. You might think it reasonable to say, “every fornicator or unclean or greedy or shameful person has no inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God.” But perhaps shamefulness lies in the one who has been stained by passion only in secret, in which state a person, even when inflamed, has held back the impulse toward fornication or uncleanness. And in what was said above, the things that bar inheritance
